overall: Atlanta is in an unusual intraday pattern — the running max of 78.8°F was recorded at midnight, with temperatures since declining to 71.6°F by 5 AM ET under a strengthening west-northwest wind. The overnight warm period appears to have been remnant warm-sector air ahead of a drying westerly flow, and the sky remains partly cloudy (FEW clouds, ~62% cloud fraction) but conditions are set up for afternoon recovery. Negative velocity and acceleration signals confirm the morning cool-down is ongoing, though afternoon solar heating under mostly sunny skies should drive a meaningful rebound.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show reasonable clustering — HRRR at 83.0°F, NBM at 82.6°F, and ECMWF slightly lower at 81.4°F — aligning closely with the NWS official high of ~83°F. The META fused model (most reliable) tells a somewhat warmer story, with its probability mass concentrated in the 84–89°F range and a weighted-mean near 85°F, diverging modestly above the NWP consensus; the INTRADAY model also peaks in the 84–87°F bins, suggesting afternoon heating may push beyond the NWP guidance.
max_temp_prediction: The day's high will almost certainly be set in the early-to-mid afternoon, needing to surpass the 78.8°F overnight running max — a threshold that all models exceed comfortably. Westerly winds of 10–15 mph will advect drier air and support strong mixing-driven surface heating under mostly sunny skies, consistent with a high in the low-to-mid 80s. Balancing the tight NWP consensus near 82–83°F against the META and INTRADAY models pointing to 84–87°F as the modal range, the best estimate is approximately 84°F with moderate confidence; a miss to the cooler side (~82°F) is plausible if cloud cover or boundary-layer mixing underperforms, while a push toward 86°F is possible if afternoon heating is vigorous.
